subject: Modularizing Shiny app and map_shape_click not working

messages.author: bebf3ffaee0e8697
messages.subject: Modularizing Shiny app and map_shape_click not working
parts:
Hello,

I am working on modularizing my Shiny app, and when I do that, there are a few things that do not work as I would expect. For example, when I click on circle markers, they no longer display the labels ('content' below). I've included pieces of the code here, but I've omitted several lines so it is hopefully easier to follow. I'm most interested in understanding the general approach I should take here. If it would be helpful, I can include all of the code. I have two main questions: 1) What should I put in the ui module if I want to have input$map_shape_click work, and 2) do I need to do anything in particular if I want to use input parameters from another module (I had a hard time following the documentation online for this). 

Thanks in advance!
SW

#ui module--------------------
DataScriptUI <- function(id){
  ns <- NS(id)
 #Not sure what to put here
}

#server module----------------
DataScript <- function(input,output,session){
  observe({ 
    leafletProxy("mapScript-map", data = zipdata)%>%  #Note that mapScript is another module I have with the leafletOutput
      addCircles(~longitude, ~latitude,radius=radius,stroke=FALSE,fillOpacity=0.5,fillColor=pal(colorData),group="Water Use")%>%
      showGroup("Water Use")%>%
      addLegend("bottomright", pal=pal,title="Withdrawal type",values=factor(colorData,labels=c("Surface Water","Groundwater","Other")), layerId="colorLegend")
  })
  
  showZipcodePopup <- function(lat, lng) {
    x1 <- as.vector(zipdata$latitude)
    x2 <- rep(lat,length(as.vector(zipdata$latitude)))
    close <- which.min(abs(x1-x2))
    selectedZip <- zipdata[close,]
      content <- as.character(tagList(
        tags$h4("Facility Information:"),
        tags$strong(HTML(sprintf("%s",
          selectedZip$city.y
        ))), tags$br(),
        sprintf("Withdrawal (MGD): %s", selectedZip$centile), tags$br(),
        sprintf("Consumption (MGD): %s", selectedZip$superzip), tags$br(),
        sprintf("Source: %s", selectedZip$college)
      ))
    leafletProxy("mapScript-map") %>% addPopups(lng, lat, content)
  }
  
  observe({
    leafletProxy("mapScript-map") %>% clearPopups()
    event <- input$map_shape_click
    if (is.null(event))
      return()
    isolate({
      showZipcodePopup(event$lat, event$lng)
    })
  })

server.r--------------------------------------------
shinyServer(function(input,output,session){
 dataFile <- callModule(DataScript,"DataScript")
})

ui.r-------------------------------------
ui <- shinyUI(navbarPage(
...
  mainPanel(
    DataScriptUI("DataScript")
  )
))

messages.author: c869f79e9e4a6b13
messages.subject: Re: Modularizing Shiny app and map_shape_click not working
parts:
I just finished creating a module for  the leaflet section of a dashboard I'm building last night.   I chose to build the module with both the UI and the server component in it.   One of things I had to do was to ensure that anytime in the UI that I was going to implement a an output, that I encapsulated the id with ns().   Example:
 
tagList(
 fluidRow(leafletOutput(ns(
 "locationSiteMap"
 ),
 height = 1024)
 , width = 12) ,
 absolutePanel(
 top = 100,
 right = 20,
 selectInput(
 ns("locationType"),
 "Location Type",
 choices = c(
 "CLINIC",
 "DEFAULT",
 "EXTERNAL",
 "HOSPITAL",
 "LAUNDRY",
 "OFFICE",
 "REMOTE"
 )
 ,
 multiple = TRUE,
 selectize = TRUE
 ) ,...

On the Server side, I also needed to make sure the right name space was used, by using session$ns(myId).  Example: 
observeEvent(input$locationSiteMap_marker_click , {
 
   
    leafletProxy(session$ns("locationSiteMap")) %>% clearPopups()
   
    isolate({
      showSitePopup(
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$id,
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$lat,
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$lng
      )
    })
  })

So ensuring that the right prefix is attached to your id is important, and requires that both the UI and the server components have this handled.  Note that this was my second module, so I'm sure you will hear more details from our experts here.
Brett

Sarah,
Is there a reason why you need to have that in a separate module?   From what I have read, it sounds like RStudio recommends that you keep interactions like this in the same module.  I am using nested modules, but the ui, and server components of each are integrated into the same module.  Hopefully some module redesign may help with this.  I'd be interested in learning where there is an exception to this.
BT
